newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan won't open Cambodia office without apology.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan won't open Cambodia office without apology.

text.p: Taiwan flatly rejected a request to reopen its unofficial office in Phnom Penh, saying this was out of the question unless Cambodian strongman Hun Sen apologised for his mistake, local newspapers reported on Sunday.
Several newspapers quoted Foreign Minister John Chang as saying Cambodia had contacted Taipei through "indirect channels", asking Taipei to reopen its office, which was shut in late July.
Chang did not say what the indirect channel was.
The newspapers quoted Chang as saying that Taipei would not agree to return to Phnom Penh unless Cambodian second prime minister Hun Sen acknowledged his mistake and apologised.

"Unless he (Hun Sen) clarifies his previous comments and apologises to us in public, our country will not return to Cambodia to set up a representative office," ruling Nationalists-owned Central Daily News quoted Chang as saying.
Hun Sen on July 22 ordered Taiwan's representative office in Phnom Penh closed, alleging Taiwanese interference in his bloody ousting of co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Taiwan, which has denied complicity in Cambodia's political turmoil, shut its office in Phnom Penh and ordered Cambodia's Taipei office closed on July 28.
With some US$130 million in investment, Taiwan's private sector ranks as the leading source of investment in Cambodia's unsteady, war-scarred economy.
Cambodia recognises only Beijing and has no official ties with Taipei.

Taiwan laid blame for the row squarely with communist China, suggesting Beijing was calling the shots in Phnom Penh and was now widening its long-time diplomatic embargo of Taipei, which it regards as a renegade province, to other non-official spheres.
Beijing has sought to squeeze Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government off the diplomatic map since it took refuge on the island after its 1949 civil war loss on the mainland.
